title: test(release): macOS smoke for released artifacts — brew core install + bd store interop
body:
## What

Adds a macOS release smoke for **released** gc artifacts — Homebrew core (bottled) install plus a bd **store interop** check — and the operator-facing procedure doc so release captains can run it before tagging.

Wasteland bounty: **w-ac31f2e263** (competing submission).

## Why

The existing `homebrew-tap-smoke.yml` validates the *first-party tap* on a macOS runner: tap install, `brew test`, `gc version`. That floor is exactly one version-string deep — and it let the v1.4.1 regression class ship:

- Bottled gc 1.4.1 embedded bd 1.2.2 while the formula depends on current beads
- On any store created/migrated by a current bd CLI (schema v66), every native store path fails: `gc mail count`, nudge delivery, session wake
- `gc version` — the only thing the tap smoke checks — passed throughout

We hit this in production (10-rig city, shared dolt server) and filed the details as #6393 (hold-label churn, maintainer-confirmed: fixes real but unreleased) and #6416 (`gc hook --claim` starvation behind the work-query probe on a serialized shared dolt server).

## The check

`macos-release-smoke.yml` (daily + dispatch, `macos-latest`):

1. `brew install gascity` — the bottled **core** artifact, not the tap
2. `gc version` — the existing floor
3. **Store interop** (the new floor): `bd init` → `gc bd list` → `gc mail count` in a temp dir. Proves the released binary's embedded bd can read a store at the current CLI's schema version. Schema skew here = the v1.4.1 class = red, with a `::error` annotation naming the likely cause and both version strings.

`engdocs/MACOS_RELEASE_SMOKE.md` documents the full release-captain procedure: brew core, goreleaser darwin artifact, the version-contains check (`git tag --contains <embedded bd>`), and a triage table mapping symptoms to #6393/#6416.

## Scope notes

- No product code touched — one workflow + one doc.
- The goreleaser-artifact half of the bounty is documented in the procedure (needs release credentials we don't assume in CI); the CI lane covers the artifact users actually install by default (Homebrew core).
- Tested the interop steps against a real v1.4.1 install before writing the workflow: bottled gc + current bd + migrated store reproduced the failure; a HEAD build with embedded bd ≥ 1.3.0 passes all three steps.

title: fix(ci): raise cmd-gc-productmetrics-testhook's timeout to fit the runner it actually gets
body:
## Summary
- Fixes #6396: `cmd-gc-productmetrics-testhook`'s `timeout-minutes: 5` was budgeting compile time, not test time -- its own timing artifact shows six tests taking 0.87s total against a 4m37 job on main, because `runner-policy` resolves `runner_32vcpu` to plain `ubuntu-latest` (4 vCPU) for every non-maintainer login, and any `go.sum` change colds the `actions/setup-go` cache and pushes the job over budget -- a hard cancellation with no failing test in the log.
- The issue proposed two fixes: (1) give the job a warm build cache, or (2) size the timeout for the runner it actually gets. Went with (2) only -- `.github/actions/setup-gascity-ubuntu` doesn't configure anything Go-cache-specific beyond what `actions/setup-go` already does inline in this job (both call the identical pinned `actions/setup-go` action); the "warm cache" effect the issue observed looks more like cache-population timing across jobs in the same workflow run, which isn't verifiable or safely restructurable without live GitHub Actions runner behavior to test against.
- Raised `timeout-minutes` to 12 -- safe, minimal, directly fixes the reported false-cancellation, and is explicitly endorsed by the issue itself as a valid stopgap.

## Test plan
- Not a Go change -- validated the YAML parses and confirmed no other docs reference the old 5-minute figure.

title: perf(gc): probe bd context once per TTL instead of once per store open (cr-uavzft)
body:
Every gc CLI call opens several stores, and each open ran the beads storage
preflight, which unconditionally forked 'bd <scope> context --json' to ask what
backend the process was about to open (cr-m3g3od measured 4 children for one
'gc bd show'). The answer - backend, dolt_mode, bd_version, schema_version - is
process-static inside any window the call lives in, so read it once per
(city, scope) and reuse it.

Only a success is recorded and the entry is aged by a TTL, so a bd that is
unreachable, uninstalled, or mid-upgrade still fails the preflight closed on
every later check, and a long-lived controller re-probes instead of carrying a
boot-time answer forever. The per-entry mutex is held across the probe, so
concurrent opens of one scope collapse into a single spawn.

Same shape gc already uses for the city-scoped storage routes
(cli_storage_routes.go), and consistent with its position on this probe in a
poll path (api_state_conditional_writes.go: 'a status poll must not shell out
to bd').

Bead: cr-uavzft
(cherry picked from commit 4d18e29d55adb25a4e6a4ee03e4d5a1b6841d198)

Staged and tested in the westlands estate (bead cr-uavzft); tests green on the estate builders.

title: cmd-gc-productmetrics-testhook runs at 92-95% of its 5-minute budget on main; its six tests take 0.87s and the rest is compile
body:
## Symptom

`cmd-gc-productmetrics-testhook` runs at 92–95% of its `timeout-minutes: 5` budget on `main`, so it fails as a cancellation ("The operation was canceled") on whichever PR happens to add a few seconds. It is a required-path job, so that reads as a red gate with no failing test in the log.

Measured across runs on 2026-09-16 (UTC):

| branch | duration |
|---|---|
| `main` @ `9700d9a48` | 4m37 |
| a branch with no `go.mod` change | 4m44 |
| a branch that changed `go.sum` | **5m05 → killed** |

## Root cause

The budget is buying compile time, not test time, on a runner the budget was not sized for.

From the job's own timing artifact (`timing-cmd-gc-productmetrics-testhook-attempt-1`, run 35040648087, `main` @ `9700d9a48`):

- `cmd/gc` package unit: **0.869 s**
- every test in it: sub-second; six tests, **0.87 s total**

against a 4m37 job. The remainder is `go build` of `cmd/gc` under `-tags productmetrics_testhook`.

The job requests `runs-on: ${{ needs.runner-policy.outputs.runner_32vcpu }}` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:626`), but `runner-policy` resolves that to `ubuntu-latest` for every login outside the maintainer list — the same artifact's runner block reports `"cpu_count": 4`. So most runs compile `cmd/gc` on four cores inside a five-minute wall.

The `go.sum` sensitivity follows: `actions/setup-go`'s cache key includes `go.sum`, so any dependency change makes that build cold, and cold is what goes over.

## Reproduction

Open a PR that changes `go.sum` at all, on a fork or from a non-maintainer login, and watch `cmd/gc product metrics testhook`. Or read the timing artifact of any recent `main` run and compare the summed test durations against the job duration.

## Environment

`main` @ `9700d9a48`, `ubuntu-latest` (4 vCPU), `actions/setup-go@4a36011`, Go per `go.mod`.

## Proposed fixes, either

1. **Give the job a warm build cache.** It is the only `cmd/gc`-building job with no warm step before it; the surrounding jobs go through `setup-gascity-ubuntu`. That attacks the 4m23 rather than the wall.
2. **Size the budget for the runner the job actually gets** — 10–12 minutes gives real margin at 4 vCPU.

(1) is the better fix; (2) is the one-line stopgap. A gate at 95% of budget reports on runner speed rather than on the code.

title: execgrace: report cooperative cancellation outcome
body:
## What changed

`execgrace.Apply` now returns a typed, concurrency-safe result that preserves the existing delivered/not-delivered contract while exposing which cancellation path ran:

- process-group interrupt
- leader-only interrupt fallback
- direct force-kill fallback
- no delivery

The runtime exec provider keeps its existing cancellation precedence through `Delivered()`. Unix and Windows signal behavior is unchanged; this adds classification and deterministic coverage for the fallback branches.

## Validation

The changed tests pass in both selecting tiers. The full local CI union, all four worker profiles in phase 1 and phase 2, acceptance A, the minimum-supported bd contract, generated-artifact freshness, build, vet, and static policy checks were run. Five unrelated environmental failures from the full union are preserved and causally attributed in the release-gate record.

title: fix(security): update grpc past GO-2026-6348
body:
## Problem

The repository-wide `govulncheck` gate began failing on otherwise unrelated PRs, including #6385, because `google.golang.org/grpc@v1.83.0` reaches GO-2026-6348. The advisory fixes that reachable HTTP/2 fragmentation OOM in v1.83.1. A second imported-package advisory, CVE-2026-84445 / GO-2026-6443, requires v1.83.2 on the 1.83 line.

## Fix

- raise the Gas City module from grpc v1.83.0 to v1.83.2;
- raise the agent image's source-built `bd` override to the same security floor;
- remove the now-obsolete `bd` and `gc` paths from both grpc Trivy waivers while retaining the still-vulnerable `gh` and `dolt` paths;
- update the existing security-policy tests so the module, container build, and waiver set remain locked together.

No application code changes.

## Verification

- RED: the same `govulncheck v1.7.0` invocation reported one reachable vulnerability, GO-2026-6348, on grpc v1.83.0.
- GREEN: `go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.7.0 -show verbose ./...` reports zero reachable or imported-package vulnerabilities on v1.83.2.
- `go mod verify`
- `go test -count=1 ./scripts`
- `go test -count=1 ./internal/warmup ./internal/events ./internal/runtime/t3bridge`
- `go vet ./...`
- repository pre-commit hook passed (lint, generated references, vet).

This is intentionally separate from #6385 so that reaper fix remains a two-file, single-purpose patch.

title: test(graph): wait on the teardown tail, not the workflow root (ga-pva49c)
body:
## What

`TestGraphWorkflowSuccessPath` used `waitForBeadClosed(workflowID)` as the barrier for three assertions about the worktree cleanup's effects: the convoy's `work_dir` being unset (`:77`), the worktree directory being removed (`:85`), and `.cleanup-worktree` appearing in the step report (`:99`). A closed workflow root does not imply any of those have happened, so the test raced the controller and went flaky under full-suite load.

Both graph workflow tests now wait on the teardown's own close via a new `waitForWorkflowTeardown` helper before asserting its effects.

## Why the root is not a barrier

Teardown-scoped work is post-settlement **by contract**, established in #5271 (bead ga-99u0u) and enforced in two places:

- `graphSinkStepIDs` (`internal/formula/graph.go`) omits `gc.scope_role=teardown` steps from `workflow-finalize`'s sinks. Sinking them deadlocks settlement — a teardown's pass condition can wait on the root outcome only finalize produces.
- `processWorkflowFinalize` (`internal/dispatch/runtime.go`) closes the root, then exempts the teardown tail from its terminal subtree sweep (`molecule.TeardownTailExclusion`) so cleanup stays executable afterwards instead of being skip-closed, which would leak the worktree.

Compiling `mol-scoped-work` shows the consequence directly:

```
workflow-finalize          <-blocks- body
workflow-finalize          <-blocks- submit-scope-check
cleanup-worktree.attempt.1 <-blocks- body
cleanup-worktree           <-blocks- body
```

`cleanup-worktree` and `workflow-finalize` are concurrent successors of the body scope with **no edge between them**. Whichever the controller reaches first wins.

The compile test's `assertBefore("…cleanup-worktree", "…workflow-finalize")` compares slice indices in the emitted recipe, not dependency edges, so it never pinned an ordering — which is why this looked guarded and was not.

The integration test was last touched 2026-06-17; the contract changed 2026-08-14 (`517b605302`) and the test was never updated. Both observed failures postdate it: ga-lwnqu9 (2026-09-04, the report assertion) and ga-qhr85l (2026-09-15, `work_dir`).

## Why the retry control is the barrier

`waitForWorkflowTeardown` waits on the cleanup step's **retry control**, not its attempt. The control closes only once the teardown has converged, so it stays correct when `attempt.1` fails transiently and `attempt.2` does the real work. The `.cleanup-worktree` ref suffix matches only that control — `.cleanup-worktree.attempt.1` and `.cleanup-worktree.spec` do not end in it. The worker writes the report line, clears `work_dir` and removes the directory *before* closing the attempt, so a closed control means all three effects are durable.

## Regression guard

`TestGraphWorkflowRootClosesWithoutTeardown` (in-memory, ~10ms, no subprocess or sleep, so no resource-census growth) pins the contract at the dispatch layer: with the teardown withheld from the worker, the root still closes `pass`, the teardown tail is still open, and the convoy still carries `work_dir`.

Verified non-vacuous — removing the teardown-sink exclusion from `graphSinkStepIDs` fails it with the root stuck `in_progress`, which is exactly the #5271 deadlock.

**No production change**: the settlement contract is deliberate and this PR does not touch it.

## Validation

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `TestGraphWorkflowSuccessPath` (tags=integration) | PASS (167.70s) |
| `TestGraphWorkflowFailureRunsCleanup` (tags=integration) | PASS (78.73s) |
| `TestGraphWorkflowRootClosesWithoutTeardown` | PASS (~10ms) |
| `make test` | PASS |
| `go vet ./...` (and `-tags integration`) | clean |
| `./internal/testpolicy/...` (resource census) | PASS |

Closes ga-pva49c. Evidence for gate tracker ga-xjh1p4.

title: fix(test): commit the transient-once budget only against a landed failure (ga-njhh8e)
body:
## What

Fixes the recurring `TestRetryManagedPooledWorkerRecoversClaimedAttemptAfterCrash`
missing-retry-attempt flake tracked by **ga-j88sfp**, which has blocked or
escalated four release gates in eight days (09-08, 09-11, 09-13, 09-15), each on
a candidate with no path overlap.

Investigation bead: ga-njhh8e.

## Root cause — the test harness, not the production retry path

`should_fail_transient_once` in `test/agents/graph-dispatch.sh` consumed its
one-shot budget **at decision time**: it wrote the marker as a side effect of
deciding to inject.

`close_with_result` deliberately swallows every `bd` error (its own comment says
so, and the rationale is sound: a transient `bd` error would otherwise kill the
worker mid-loop under `set -e`). So when the failing close did not land, the
attempt bead stayed open with the budget already spent. The next pass over that
bead saw the marker, declined to inject, fell through to the normal path, and
closed the attempt `gc.outcome=pass`. `classifyRetryAttempt` then reads a clean
pass, correctly schedules no retry, and the workflow finalizes pass with only
`.attempt.1`.

That is exactly the observed shape in all four sightings: `.attempt.1` present,
`.attempt.2` absent, workflow pass.

**The production side is correct throughout.** Given an attempt closed pass with
no failure metadata, `internal/dispatch/retry.go:416` declining to retry is the
right behavior. Real retries are not being lost. The harness was mislabeling a
failed attempt as a passing one. The `transient-once` pattern has no production
analogue — it exists only under `test/`.

## Fix

Split the decision from the commit:

- `should_fail_transient_once` is now a pure predicate with no side effect.
- `commit_transient_once` writes the marker, and the main loop calls it only
  after reading back `status=closed outcome=fail`.

A dropped close now leaves the budget owed so the next pass re-injects; a landed
close still spends it exactly once.

## Diagnostics

The missing-attempt assertion now dumps workflow state. A real gate failure
previously carried only the step list — the entire `ga-3r36gw` recovery log is
592 bytes, one assertion line, no worker trace. That ambiguity (a lost injection
and a controller that declined to retry look identical) is why this stayed
unrooted across four sightings. The new `transient-once-uncommitted` trace line
names a dropped close directly.

## Evidence

- Regression test `TestGraphDispatchTransientOnceBudgetSurvivesLostClose`
  extracts the real shell functions and pins all three properties: budget
  survives a close that never landed, budget is spent once the close lands,
  unselected refs are never injected.
- Verified RED against the pre-fix source and GREEN after: two decisions with no
  landed close leave the injection owed under the fix, and lose it before it.
- Alternative hypothesis disproved: "the attempt-1 outcome is recorded pass
  before the transient injection takes effect" is structurally impossible —
  `should_fail_transient_once` is consulted *before* any pass-close path in the
  same loop iteration and `continue`s past it. The only route to `.attempt.1`
  closing pass is a previously-consumed marker.

## Scope

Covers **ga-j88sfp** only. Two other open trackers on the same test are distinct
conditions and are explicitly **not** addressed here:

- **ga-oc46fi** — `.attempt.2` did materialize; the trace lacked the success
  entry. Different phase.
- **ga-tot0gw** — `gc init` colliding with an incompatible active supervisor.
  Environmental.

## Census

The new test executes the real shell functions through one `bash` subprocess —
the same idiom the sibling `TestGraphDispatchHookFallbackForNamedWorker` already
uses in this file — so the all-source subprocess census grows by one call (file
count unchanged; the file already spawns). Pinned in the three places the
manifest header requires to move together: the Go `bootstrapPolicy`,
`test-resources.toml`, and the generated `TESTING.md` row.

## Testing

- `TestGraphDispatchTransientOnceBudgetSurvivesLostClose` passes (3 subtests).
- Pre-existing `TestGraphDispatchHookFallbackForNamedWorker` still passes.
- `go vet -tags integration ./test/integration/` clean.
- `shellcheck -S warning` on the script reports only a pre-existing SC2034 at
  line 453, outside this diff.
- Full pre-push suite green.

**Not verified locally:** the live integration test cannot run in this
environment — it fails at `bd init` on the pending Dolt schema migration
(ga-3jtbpm). Confirmed environmental by running it at clean `origin/main` in a
scratch worktree: identical failure, same point. CI exercises it properly.

title: fix(worktree): stop TestManagedDryRunDoesNotPublishProvenance flaking on transient git lock files
body:
## What

`TestManagedDryRunDoesNotPublishProvenance` byte-compares a `snapshotTree` walk of a test repo's common git dir before and after a dry-run, to prove the dry-run touched nothing. Git's own background maintenance can create and remove `objects/maintenance.lock` inside that window, independent of anything the code under test did — either direction (appearing or disappearing between the two walks) fails the assertion.

Fixes #6175.

## Fix

Both of the following, since they're complementary, not competing:

- `initTestRepo` (the package-local wrapper, not the shared `testutil.InitGitRepo`) now sets `maintenance.auto=false` and `gc.auto=0` on every test repo, so no background maintenance runs against fixture repos in this package at all — root cause, and it protects every other `snapshotTree`-based purity assertion in the package, not just this one test.
- `snapshotTree` itself now filters `*.lock` files out of its walk — a second, belt-and-braces layer in case some other lock-taking git operation ever runs against a fixture repo.

**New test proves the filter, not just the theory:** `TestSnapshotTreeExcludesLockFiles` seeds a durable file plus a transient lock file inside an already-existing `objects/` dir (matching a real git repo's shape, not a synthetic new directory) and asserts the lock file never shows up in a before/after diff. Verified it actually catches the regression: temporarily disabled the filter and confirmed the test fails with exactly the shape #6175 describes, then restored.

## Testing

`go build -tags gms_pure_go ./internal/worktree/...` clean. Full `internal/worktree` package suite passes (including the new test and the originally-flaky test). `gofmt -l` on the touched file is empty.

title: fix(tmuxtest): escalate past a failed kill-server when reaping orphan servers (post-merge remediation for #6296)
body:
Post-merge review remediation for #6296.

## Why this is a follow-up PR and not a revert

#6296 squash-merged as `a1deacc6` while the remediation for its pre-merge
review's `request_changes` findings was still being written. The remediation
commit `1ecde94d` was authored 89 seconds *after* the merge and never reached
the branch — `git log --all --find-object` finds the landed
`test/tmuxtest/orphan_sweep.go` blob (`cd3ff9c9`) in exactly one commit, the
merge itself. That blob matches neither the gated tree nor the authored
remediation, so this was not a merge-queue race against an already-pushed
approved head.

The post-merge review of the landed range re-raised those findings
(decision `request_changes`, quality score 791/1000 against a 850 threshold).
This PR carries the remediation onto `main`. The merge is not undone.

## Findings addressed

| ID | Severity | Category | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| NF-1 | **major** | Error Handling & Resilience | Fixed |
| NF-2 | **major** | Release Safety | Fixed (addendum, not SHA rewrite — see below) |
| NF-3 | minor | Security Surface | Fixed; optional increment declined with recorded reason |
| NF-4 | minor | Contract & Interface Fidelity | Fixed |
| NF-5 | minor | Resource Lifecycle & Cleanup | Fixed + regression lock |
| NF-6 | minor | Debuggability & Operability | Fixed |
| NF-7 | minor | Test Evidence Quality | Fixed |
| NF-8 | nit | Architectural Consistency | Fixed |
| NF-9 | nit | Resource Lifecycle & Cleanup | Fixed |
| NF-10 | nit | Architectural Consistency | Fixed |

### NF-1 — the fail-open kill (the defect that matters)

`killTmuxServersUnder` returned as soon as `tmux kill-server` failed:

```go
if _, err := exec.CommandContext(killCtx, "tmux", "-S", path, "kill-server").CombinedOutput(); err != nil {
    return nil // skips the exit poll, the SIGKILL, and every diagnostic
}
```

The caller unlinks the socket either way, so the failure arm was precisely the
one that could leave a server running, socketless, and undiscoverable — the
`ga-t33q83` symptom the sweep exists to prevent. `reapServerAtSocket` now
escalates on every arm and names each outcome on `diagnostics`.

### NF-2 — the release gate record

`release-gates/ga-47b6fl-tmux-orphan-sweep-gate.md` presents a PASS whose
reviewed SHA is not what landed. **Both cited SHAs are real and accurately
name the 2026-09-11 run**, verified first-hand: `1dacc4f3d6` exists and its
`test/tmuxtest` tree is identical to the gated `62cc46d8cc`'s; `41edfbef91` is
on `main`. They are left unchanged and an addendum records that the gate's
PASS does not extend to the merged head.

Rewriting them to the merged head would assert that the 40-job local CI union,
its preserved logs, and its five failure attributions were collected against
content they never saw. The finding's intent — a reader must not believe the
landed state was gated — is satisfied without falsifying an audit record.

### NF-3 — authenticating the signal target

The SIGKILL target is now re-attributed before it is signaled: same PID, same
start time (`pidutil.AliveWithStartTime`), still `argv[0]` basename `tmux`
(`pidutil.AliveWithCmdline`), never this process. The PID comes from an IPC
peer discovered under a shared socket root and may be up to
`killTmuxServerWait` stale by the time the signal lands, so bare liveness was
enough to kill a recycled PID's innocent new owner.

**Not applied — NF-3's optional increment** (veto the SIGKILL when no
start-time token is available). `pidutil.StartTime` reads `/proc`, so it fails
for *every* PID on darwin; the veto would delete the escalation entirely on
macOS hosts, where an orphaned server is just as able to outlive
`kill-server`. The token is one of two independent gates, and the other keeps
narrowing the target on Linux when the token is missing. The reasoning is
recorded on `reapServerAtSocket`.

### NF-5 — the one finding the authored remediation did not fix

The sweep regression test's cleanup issued an unbounded `exec.Command`
`kill-server` against a server the sweep under test may have left wedged,
hanging the whole package until the outer `go test` timeout with no output
(every call site passes `io.Discard`). It now routes through the bounded
`killTmuxServerAtSocket`, falling back to a direct PID kill of the exact
server this test spawned and verified — never a bare or default-socket
`kill-server`.

`TestEveryKillServerCallIsBounded` (new) parses this package's sources and
pins the rule so the shape cannot return. It is AST-based rather than a grep
so the `"tmux kill-server"` string literal in `orphan_sweep_reaper_test.go` is
not a false positive, and it fails if it finds zero `.go` files so the scan
cannot go vacuous.

### NF-4 / NF-6 / NF-7 / NF-8 / NF-9 / NF-10

- **NF-4** — `SweepOrphanPIDPrefixedDirs` and `NewSocketParentDir` now
  document that they signal processes, not just remove directories.
- **NF-6** — every reap outcome (unreapable socket, self-PID refusal, failed
  `kill-server`, graceful exit, no-longer-tmux, failed SIGKILL, successful
  SIGKILL) is named on `diagnostics`, so a survivor stays attributable from
  run logs instead of gate-log forensics.
- **NF-7** — `TestReapServerAtSocketEscalation` drives all eight escalation
  paths through a fake host, including the load-bearing *"kill-server failed,
  server survives"* row that no fixture can produce on demand.
  `TestIsTmuxArgv` covers the argv gate.
- **NF-8 / NF-10** — the monolithic `killTmuxServersUnder` is split behind the
  `tmuxServerReaper` seam (the shape
  `internal/runtime/proctable/kill_unix.go` already uses to test its own
  confirmed-dead-before-return guarantee), and `killTestSocketPath` becomes
  `killTmuxServerAtSocket`, which reports *why* a shutdown failed instead of
  discarding the error.
- **NF-9** — a socket reporting this process as its own tmux server is refused
  rather than signaled.

## Resource census ledger

The NF-5 fix *removes* an `exec.Command` tmux call, so
`TestRepositoryLedgerMatchesCensusAndDocumentation` reported the baselines as
stale-high ("lower the checked baseline to bank the improvement"). All four
synchronized surfaces drop exactly one subprocess/tmux call — `census.go`,
`census_test.go`, `test/test-resources.toml`, and `TESTING.md`. File counts
are unchanged: the two new test files use no resources.

## Test evidence

All green with `-count=1`, no unexpected skips:

- `TestReapServerAtSocketEscalation` (8 rows), `TestIsTmuxArgv` (6 rows)
- `TestEveryKillServerCallIsBounded`
- `TestSweepOrphanPIDPrefixedDirsKillsLiveTmuxServerBeforeRemoval` — the
  real-tmux end-to-end case; **ran, did not skip**
- `internal/testpolicy/resourcecensus` — full package
- `gofmt -l` empty, `go vet` clean, pre-commit lint `0 issues`

**Mutation-probed** — both load-bearing fixes are pinned by a test that
actually fails without them:

| Mutant | Expected | Observed |
|---|---|---|
| Restore the NF-1 fail-open `return` | NF-1 row RED | `FAIL TestReapServerAtSocketEscalation/kill-server_failed,_server_survives` |
| Restore the NF-5 unbounded call | NF-5 lock RED | `FAIL TestEveryKillServerCallIsBounded` at `orphan_sweep_tmux_test.go:75:7` |
| Clean tree (control) | green | `ok` |

The NF-5 mutant had to be applied on disk rather than through `go test
-overlay`: the lock reads the package's sources with `os.ReadDir` at run time,
and `-overlay` only redirects what the *compiler* sees, so an overlay mutant
silently passes against the real unmutated file.

title: test: pin LC_ALL/LANG=C.UTF-8 in hermetic test env for deterministic git messages
body:
## Summary

- Pins `LANG=C.UTF-8` and `LC_ALL=C.UTF-8` in all four hermetic test-environment locations so `git` always emits English messages, fixing assertion failures on non-English build hosts (e.g. a German-locale Debian host with translated git message catalogs installed).
- Keeps the four env locations in lockstep, as required by the repo's _Hermetic Git test config is mirrored_ rule (Makefile `TEST_ENV` + the three nested `env -i` wrappers in `scripts/test-{go-test,integration}-shard` and `scripts/test-local-parallel`).

### Why it's needed
The `env -i` test wrappers previously forwarded the host `LANG` (only defaulting to `C.UTF-8` when unset) and never set `LC_ALL`. On a non-English host, git emitted localized error text, breaking tests that assert on English substrings:

- `internal/doctor` — `TestBeadsRoleCheck_Fix_PreservesReadFailureContext` (`"bad config line 1"` vs `"Ungültige Konfigurationszeile 1"`)
- `internal/packman` — `TestDefaultRunGitBlocksDisallowedTransport` (`"not allowed"` vs `"nicht erlaubt"`)

`debian/rules` already sets `LANG=C LC_ALL=C` for `make test`, but `TEST_ENV`'s `env -i` allowlist dropped `LC_ALL` and re-forwarded the host `LANG`, and the parallel runner / shard wrappers forwarded the host `LANG` directly — so the intended C locale never reached the git subprocess. `C.UTF-8` forces English git messages while preserving UTF-8 byte semantics.

## Testing

- [x] `bash -n` syntax-checked `scripts/test-go-test-shard`, `scripts/test-integration-shard`, `scripts/test-local-parallel`; reviewed the Makefile `TEST_ENV` block.
- [ ] `make check`
- [ ] `make check-docs` if docs, navigation, or links changed _(no docs changed)_
- [ ] `make test-integration` if runtime, controller, or workflow behavior changed _(test-runner env only; no runtime change)_

## Checklist

- [x] Linked an issue, or explained why one is not needed — no tracker issue existed for this; the failing assertions were reproduced directly on a non-English build host.
- [x] Added or updated tests for behavior changes — this **is** the fix for two existing tests that fail under a non-C locale; no new test added (pinning the hermetic env is the corrective measure).
- [x] Updated docs for user-facing changes — no user-facing change.

title: test(cmd/gc): raise canned leak-guard PIDs above pid_max
body:
## Summary

`TestRequireNoLeakedDoltAfter_MultipleLeaksReportedSorted` feeds canned fake PIDs (`50001`/`50002`) through `requireNoLeakedDoltAfterWith`, which asserts exactly **one** aggregated `Errorf`. The cleanup then reaps the leaked PIDs via `reapDoltLeakPIDsWithKiller`, whose waiter polls `processStillAlive` (`kill -0`) until each PID exits or a 5 s deadline elapses (added in #5402).

On a shared host those low canned PIDs can collide with real processes owned by another user/namespace: `ps` cannot see them, but `kill -0` returns success, so `processStillAlive` reports them alive forever. The reaper times out twice and emits two extra `test leaked dolt cleanup failed: pid N still alive after SIGKILL …` errors, taking the test from the expected 1 `Errorf` to 3 and failing the single-aggregation assertion.

## Fix

Move the canned PIDs to `5000001`/`5000002`, above Linux's default `/proc/sys/kernel/pid_max` (`4194304`), so they can never collide with a live host process. The test's sorting/aggregation guarantees are unchanged; only the fixture PIDs and the matching `strings.Index` literals move.

## Why not the other low canned PIDs in the file?

Sibling tests using `1000`/`1001`/`9999`/etc. either route through `requireNoLeakedDoltAfterWithFilterAndKiller` with tolerant assertions (`strings.Contains`, not an exact error count) or exercise the enumerator/filter/snapshot logic without the production-waiter reap, so they do not flake on phantom aliveness. This change is surgical to the one test whose `len(inner.errors) != 1` assertion is broken by the collision.

## Testing

- Targeted test reproduced red before the change (3 errors instead of 1 on a host where PIDs 50001/50002 are live in another namespace).
- After: `go test -run TestRequireNoLeakedDoltAfter_MultipleLeaksReportedSorted ./cmd/gc/` passes **5 consecutive runs**.
- Full leak-helper + reaper suite green: `go test -run 'TestRequireNoLeakedDoltAfter|TestReapDoltLeakPIDs' ./cmd/gc/`.
- `go vet ./cmd/gc/` clean.

title: fix(residency): re-key the infra_class_migrate baseline row the s4/s8 squashes left disagreeing
body:
## What

`main` is red on the residency boundary guard. This re-keys one baseline
row. No Go code changes.

## The failure

On `origin/main` at `fc7a23a292` (verified on an untouched export),
`./scripts/check-residency-boundary.sh` exits 1 with a matched grow/shrink
pair on a single file:

```
RESIDENCY-BOUNDARY: cmd/gc/infra_class_migrate.go infraBindingIDPrefix d:ReservedClassPrefix: 1 sites, baseline 0 — a NEW store-enumeration site. Consume internal/storeref (Plan/ResolveOwner/Union) or annotate the line with `// residency:allow <reason>`.
RESIDENCY-BOUNDARY: cmd/gc/infra_class_migrate.go openInfraDestination d:ReservedClassPrefix: 0 sites, baseline 1 — the baseline must SHRINK in the same commit that retires a site. Follow the regeneration procedure in the header of scripts/residency-boundary-baseline.txt; do NOT redirect --emit-baseline over that file, it emits this half' rows only.
```

After this PR:

```
$ ./scripts/check-residency-boundary.sh; echo $?
0
$ ./scripts/check-residency-boundary.sh --self-test; echo $?
0
```

## Why it broke: two squashes, one minute apart

Neither PR added a blind reader. The census key the guard pins is
`(path, function, pattern)`, so moving a call between functions **in the
same file** re-keys the row even when the call itself is untouched — and
the guard reports that as a simultaneous grow and shrink.

- **#5643 (s4, squash `7746bbe5ab`, merged 15:27Z)** stopped allowlisting
  `cmd/gc/infra_class_migrate.go` and pinned its single
  `config.ReservedClassPrefix` call in the baseline, attributed to
  `openInfraDestination` — the function that held it on that PR's base.
- **#5597 (s8, squash `fc7a23a292`, merged 15:28Z, one minute later)** had
  already extracted that call into a new helper, `infraBindingIDPrefix`,
  on **its** base.

Each PR was green against the base it was tested on. The merged result is
s4's baseline row describing a function layout s8 had replaced. Nothing in
either change is wrong; the two squashes simply disagree about where the
call lives.

## The fix

The file still makes exactly one hit, in exactly one function
(`infraBindingIDPrefix`, `cmd/gc/infra_class_migrate.go:594`), so the fix
is the baseline row, not the code:

```diff
-cmd/gc/infra_class_migrate.go	openInfraDestination	d:ReservedClassPrefix	1
+cmd/gc/infra_class_migrate.go	infraBindingIDPrefix	d:ReservedClassPrefix	1
```

That is the **entire** diff: 114 rows before, 114 after, no other row
moves and none drops, so the shrink-only ratchet is not loosened. The
header prose that pins these rows — "Six rows, six hits" across
`residency_topology.go`, `infra_class_migrate.go` and `cmd_storage.go` —
still counts correctly (4 + 1 + 1), and no header block names the
function by spelling, so no prose changes with the row.

Regenerated by the documented three-emitter splice in the baseline's own
header, not by redirecting `--emit-baseline` over the file (which would
have dropped the two AST halves and the hand-written header): the shell
half with its four `# PARTIAL:` warning lines dropped, plus both
`RESIDENCY_BASELINE_EMIT=1 go test ./scripts` emitters filtered with
`awk -F'\t' 'NF==4'` to strip the harness chatter, concatenated and put
through one `LC_ALL=C sort`.

## Gates

| command | exit |
| --- | --- |
| `./scripts/check-residency-boundary.sh` | 0 |
| `./scripts/check-residency-boundary.sh --self-test` | 0 |
| `go test ./scripts/... -count=1` (AST ratchet) | 0 — `ok` |
| `go build ./...` | 0 |
| `go vet ./...` | 0 |
| `make check-docs` | 0 |
| `make test-fast-parallel` | 0 — `All fast jobs passed` |

Refs ga-j4p3y

title: feat(beads): default managed scopes to proxied Dolt
body:
Flips the default Dolt mode for **freshly created managed scopes** to Beads'
`proxied-server` path, adds an external Unix-socket front door for proxied
Dolt, and moves the `bd` pin to `v1.3.0-rc.1`. The original scope of this
branch — deterministic external Unix-socket front-door outage/recovery
coverage plus a direct/proxy parity matrix that asserts no managed Dolt
runtime is created — is retained.

Retitled from `test(beads): harden external proxy topology outage/reconnect`:
the branch carries production-path changes that a `test(...)` scope hides from
reviewers and from changelog/release-note tooling.

## Production-path changes

### 1. Proxied-server is the default for new managed scopes

`desiredCityDoltConfigState` / `desiredRigDoltConfigState` now select
`dolt_mode=proxied-server` for a fresh managed scope. An explicit external
host/port endpoint still selects direct `server` mode.

**Existing scopes are not migrated.** `resolveDesired*EndpointState` resolves
persisted authoritative scope state before these constructors run, so an
already-initialized workspace keeps the mode it recorded
(`TestResolveDesiredCityEndpointStatePreservesAuthoritativeDoltMode`).
Converting an existing scope is an explicit, journalled operator step — see
`engdocs/contributors/beads-proxy-migration.md`.

### 2. The `bd` pin moves to the `v1.3.0-rc.1` prerelease

`deps.env:BD_VERSION`, the `go.mod` beads library pin, and
`contrib/k8s/Dockerfile.agent:BD_VERSION` all move `v1.1.0` → `v1.3.0-rc.1`.

GitHub marks `v1.3.0-rc.1` a **prerelease**. Pointing the installable default
at a prerelease is a deliberate exception to the published-release bar this pin
otherwise holds, taken because the RC is the first main-cut tag carrying the
per-subcommand flags this branch depends on. Move `BD_VERSION` to the first
non-prerelease release cut from beads `main` once one exists. The caveat is
recorded at `deps.env:29-33`.

### 3. Migration ordering requirement (v53 → v66 schema)

`BD_VERSION` and the `go.mod` library pin **must move together**. gc both links
beads as a library and shells out to `bd`, so a lagging half locks the other
out: after the v53 → v66 schema migration an older co-resident `bd` refuses the
store under the forward schema-skew guard.

Ordering for a shared, no-remote Dolt sql-server (this repo's shape):

1. Upgrade **every** `bd` client to `v1.3.0-rc.1` first. bd >= 1.3.0
   deliberately refuses to auto-apply pending migrations here, because
   migrating would lock out every co-resident client still on the old schema.
2. Only then run `bd migrate schema` **once**, from a designated migrator.
3. Do not work around a pending-migration refusal with `bd dolt pull` or an
   ad-hoc `BD_ALLOW_REMOTE_MIGRATE=1`.

This is the axis a `test(...)` title would not have prompted anyone to plan.

### 4. Unix-socket front door for external proxied Dolt

Dolt connection targets are socket-aware end to end: an external socket
endpoint is carried through config resolution and projected into child `bd`
processes, and the managed-Dolt socket handle is pooled.

## Test coverage

Deterministic external Unix-socket front-door outage/recovery coverage,
assertions that an external socket creates no managed Dolt runtime, and a
direct-vs-proxied front-door parity matrix across `proxied-managed`,
`proxied-external-host`, and `proxied-external-socket`.

title: test(gc): characterise the desired-state freeze on a store-unavailable scope
body:
Part of the split of the closed #3324 into independently reviewable pieces. Wave two. Based on `main`; stands alone.

## Why this exists

A scope whose bead store is unreachable reports zero ready work. Nothing in the reconciler distinguishes that from a genuinely empty queue, so the failure mode is a silent flatten to zero demand: the pool drains on a store outage, and the work is rediscovered a tick later, after the seats are gone.

The machinery that prevents this **already exists on `main`** — `defaultScaleCheckCounts` marks a template partial when its store read fails, and `retainScaleCheckPartialPoolDesired` freezes a partial template's desired count at the number of currently-running sessions. What did not exist was a test saying so, which makes it exactly the kind of behaviour a refactor removes without anything going red.

This is a characterisation PR: no production change beyond the typed sentinel the tests are expressed in.

## What it does

Two tests in a new `cmd/gc/build_desired_state_unavailable_test.go`:

**Scope quarantine.** A store that fails `Ready` with the typed unavailable error marks *its own* template partial and surfaces a diagnostic, while a healthy sibling scope still counts its work normally. The invariant is that one scope's outage does not stall the fleet — and equally, that the unavailable scope does not silently vanish from the error list.

**The freeze, with its negative.** Retention freezes the unavailable scope at its running-session count. The same zero-count input *without* the partial marking still drains to nothing. The negative half is the point: it shows the partial signal is what arms the freeze, so the test cannot pass by accident on an implementation that retains everything unconditionally.

## Verified to bite

Both were confirmed red against deliberate breakage before being proposed:

- making `markScaleCheckPartialTemplate` a no-op fails the quarantine test;
- short-circuiting the retention guard fails the freeze test.

Both restored green.

## Carried helper

`internal/beads.ErrStoreUnavailable` is the typed sentinel the tests express "unavailable" in, and it does not exist on `main` yet. The identical 8-line declaration is also carried by **#5949** (bd admission semaphore) and by the `gc hook` exit-2 PR — same file, same text, no semantic divergence. Whichever lands first, the others' copies drop out. Flagging it so it does not read as a real conflict. Nothing else here depends on those PRs.

## What it does NOT do

- No production behaviour change. `build_desired_state.go` is untouched.
- Does not make anything *return* `ErrStoreUnavailable` in production — the store layer that does is a separate piece. These tests inject a fake store that returns it, which is what lets them pin the reconciler's reaction independently of who produces the signal.
- Does not cover the API/dashboard projection of a degraded scope.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./cmd/gc/ ./internal/beads/`, `gofmt -l` — clean
- `GC_FAST_UNIT=0 go test ./cmd/gc/ -run 'TestDefaultScaleCheckCountsStoreUnavailableQuarantinesOneScope|TestRetainScaleCheckPartialPoolDesiredFreezesUnavailableScope' -v` — 2 tests, both pass
- pre-push gauntlet (`test-local-parallel fast`, all 6 `cmd/gc` shards + core) — all jobs passed

title: test(resilience): injectable jitter seam for deterministic breaker backoff
body:
Part of the twelve-way split of the closed #3324.

## Why this exists

`Breaker` already carries an injectable `jitter` field, but `Registry` — the
only public way to obtain a breaker — has no way to reach it. Every consumer
of a registry-owned breaker therefore gets a uniform draw from `(0, cap]` for
its open-state deadline, which makes any test that asserts on a backoff
deadline time-dependent. `Registry.SetJitterForTest` pins the jitter function
on the registry and on every breaker it has already handed out, exactly the
way `SetOnStateChange` already reaches both.

## What it does not do

Nothing about the default. An unpinned registry keeps full jitter; a test
guards that, because silently losing full jitter would remove the
thundering-herd protection the backoff exists for. No production caller is
added — the consumers that motivate this seam (the bd chokepoint breaker and
its timeout classification) are separate PRs in the same split.

## Stacking

None. This applies to current `origin/main` on its own.

## Extraction fidelity

`internal/resilience/registry.go` is taken verbatim from the fork:
`git diff fork/main -- internal/resilience/registry.go` is empty.

`internal/resilience/registry_jitter_test.go` is new and written for this PR —
the fork has no test for this seam because its only callers are `cmd/gc` tests
that live in later slices. Flagging that explicitly so it is not mistaken for
extracted code.

## Verification

```
gofmt -l internal/resilience/                      clean
go vet ./internal/resilience/                      clean
golangci-lint run ./internal/resilience/...        0 issues
go test ./internal/resilience/ -count=1 -v         31 PASS, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP (0s)
go test ./internal/resilience/ -race -count=1      ok (1.0s)
```

Both new guards were checked by breaking what they guard:

- deleting `b.jitter = r.jitter` from `Registry.Breaker` →
  `TestRegistrySetJitterForTestPinsNewBreakers` fails
  (`open backoff = 254.137761ms, want exactly 1s`)
- deleting the existing-breaker loop from `SetJitterForTest` →
  `TestRegistrySetJitterForTestPinsExistingBreakers` fails
  (`open backoff = 1.794389616s, want exactly 2s`)

title: internal/api/dashboardspa/dist has non-deterministic content hashes across CI/build runs, causing repeated rename/rename conflicts
body:
## Summary

`internal/api/dashboardspa/dist` (the committed, CI-enforced dashboard bundle regenerated by `make dashboard-build`) appears to get different Vite content-hashed filenames across separate builds of the same source, even with zero dashboard-source changes in between. This has caused the same rename/rename conflict to recur repeatedly on unrelated PRs whose branch happens to rebuild `dist/` at a different point than `main`'s own copy.

## What we observed

While preparing #5854 (a small, generated-artifacts-only PR — the API-schema-regen half of the #4878 split), the branch went `CONFLICTING` a second time after already having been rebuilt and pushed clean once. Investigating:

- Every file in `dist/` showed as a `rename/rename` conflict against `main`.
- The *other* generated artifacts this PR touches (`docs/reference/schema/openapi.json`/`.txt`, both generated API clients, `internal/api/huma_types_sessions.go`) were byte-identical between this branch's merge-base and current `main` — no drift there.
- Only `dist/`'s content-hashed filenames had moved on `main` in the interim, despite no dashboard source change landing between those two points.

This is the second time this exact shape has shown up (see also #4878's original diff-size investigation and the #5854/#4878 split it produced) — earlier investigation in that thread confirmed `make dashboard-build` is deterministic *within* one local environment (4 repeated builds, zero drift, same machine) but *not* across environments/runs, consistent with Vite/Rollup's content-hashing being sensitive to something that varies between build invocations (dependency resolution order, environment, or similar) rather than the source input itself.

## Why this matters

Any PR that legitimately needs to touch `dist/` (a real dashboard source change) is effectively racing `main`'s own build non-determinism: rebase, rebuild, push — and by the time it's reviewed, `main` may have rebuilt `dist/` again on its own (via CI or another merge) with different hashes for functionally identical output, producing a spurious full-tree conflict on next rebase. This isn't something a contributor can fix from their own branch; it needs someone with visibility into the actual CI build environment to look at whether the Vite/Rollup build can be made to produce stable content hashes for identical source (e.g. pinned dependency resolution, a fixed build seed/mode, or a lockstep regen step that only CI runs).

## Not filing as a "fix this" — filing as a build-pipeline observation

We don't have visibility into what specifically varies between builds (this repo's Node/Vite toolchain, or how CI triggers `dashboard-build`), so this is reported as an observed pattern with the evidence above, not a diagnosed root cause. Happy to help verify a hypothesis if a maintainer has a theory about what's actually varying.

title: fix(test): leak-guard reap probes an injected liveness, not the real process table
body:
## Bug

`TestRequireNoLeakedDoltAfter_MultipleLeaksReportedSorted` fabricated PIDs
50001/50002 and drove the leak guard with the no-op killer
`ignoreProcessSignal` — but the guard's reap hardcoded the **real** liveness
prober `processStillAlive` (`syscall.Kill(pid, 0)`). The killer and the prober
are two halves of one reaper; splitting them meant the guard signalled nothing
while still polling the real process table for pids it had invented.

When a fabricated pid names a live process on the host, the reap therefore
spins its full 5s deadline and appends a `cleanup failed` `Errorf` per pid,
breaking the "exactly one aggregated Errorf" assertion:

```
--- FAIL: TestRequireNoLeakedDoltAfter_MultipleLeaksReportedSorted (5.09s)
    dolt_leak_helper_test.go:211: multiple leaks must be aggregated into one Errorf, got 3
      ... pid 50001 still alive after SIGKILL and 5s wait (leak-guard reap timed out)
      ... pid 50002 still alive after SIGKILL and 5s wait (leak-guard reap timed out)
```

This is not flaky — it stays red for as long as the pid range is occupied. On
the reporting host `/proc/50001` and `/proc/50002` were both live `dolt`
children of one sql-server, so `make test-fast-parallel` failed deterministically
and blocked every push. Previously seen on CI as run 32587221748 (cmd/gc shard
12 of 12).

## Fix

Inject the whole reaper instead of just its killer, so the two halves cannot
be mismatched by construction:

- `requireNoLeakedDoltAfterWithFilterAndKiller(..., killFn)` becomes
  `requireNoLeakedDoltAfterWithFilterAndReaper(..., reap func([]int) []error)`.
  The guard's only use of `killFn` was to hand it to the reaper, so there is
  no longer a seam that accepts one half alone.
- Production (`requireNoLeakedDoltAfterForPaths`) passes `reapDoltLeakPIDs`,
  which pairs `killProcess` with `processStillAlive` at the production
  poll/deadline bounds — identical behaviour to before.
- Scripted-pid guards pass `scriptedDoltLeakReaper(fakeKiller)`, which pairs
  the fake killer with the new `processNeverAlive`. No test path consults the
  real process table for a fabricated pid any more.
- `reapDoltLeakPIDsWithKiller` and `reapDoltLeakProcessesWithKiller` are gone:
  both were "injectable killer + hardcoded real prober", the exact shape of
  this bug, and every remaining caller passed the real `killProcess`.

Defense in depth: fabricated pids now come from `unallocatablePIDs(t, n)`,
which reads `/proc/sys/kernel/pid_max` and returns `pid_max+1 …`. The kernel
never allocates above that ceiling, so collision is impossible by
construction. With the probe injected a collision no longer changes any
outcome; this guards a future call site that re-pairs a fake killer with the
real prober.

Control kept: `TestRequireNoLeakedDoltAfterReportsStillAlivePIDAsCleanupFailure`
drives the guard with a probe that reports the pid alive after SIGKILL and
pins that the aggregation still emits one leak `Errorf` **plus** a separate
cleanup-failure `Errorf` naming the pid — so swapping in `processNeverAlive`
cannot silence a genuine reap failure.

## RED → GREEN

Before, on a host where 50001/50002 are live:

```
--- FAIL: TestRequireNoLeakedDoltAfter_MultipleLeaksReportedSorted (5.09s)
    dolt_leak_helper_test.go:211: multiple leaks must be aggregated into one Errorf, got 3
```

After: `--- PASS ... (0.25s)` — a 5.09s stall becomes 0.25s.

`go test ./cmd/gc -run 'DoltLeak|LeakedDolt|RequireNoLeaked' -count=1 -v` →
**19 `--- PASS`, 0 FAIL, 0 SKIP.**

Both new probes are load-bearing, verified by mutation:

| Mutation | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `processNeverAlive` → `return true` | `MultipleLeaksReportedSorted` fails with the original text: `multiple leaks must be aggregated into one Errorf, got 3` + `still alive after SIGKILL` |
| control's `neverDies` → `return false` | control fails with `expected one aggregated leak Errorf plus one cleanup-failure Errorf, got 1` |

The two mutations fail differently, so neither test is vacuous.

## Gates

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `go build ./cmd/gc` | pass |
| `go vet ./cmd/gc` | pass |
| `gofmt -l cmd/gc/` | clean |
| `golangci-lint run ./cmd/gc/...` | 0 issues |
| `./scripts/check-residency-boundary.sh` | pass (exit 0) |
| `make test-fast-parallel` | pass (green via the pre-push hook: all 10 jobs, `unit-core` + all 6 `unit-cmd-gc` shards) |

One earlier `make test-fast-parallel` run failed on
`internal/productmetrics/TestRecordOnceKeepsStoredEventWhenSpawnWindowExpires`,
a package this branch does not touch (`git diff origin/main...HEAD` is three
`cmd/gc/*_test.go` files). It passes 5/5 in isolation and passed on the
pre-push rerun; it is a wall-clock `defaultRecordDecisionBudget` flake under
16-way parallelism. Filed separately as `ga-2rlkv`.

Refs ga-ay6x1
